This is an experimental port from a C# server/database application — to a GitHub repo/VS Code extension. A concept driven by transformational conversations with a robotics firm — HAL Robotics.

This site is built with Docs Assembler and hosted on GitHub Pages. You can view the source code and documentation structure in the Docs Assembler Demo repo.

Tame Documentation Hell

Docs Assembler enables you to build documentation like Lego. Capture complex thinking, simplify intricate systems into a single source of truth. A unified, validated, maintainable decision system that can guide an entire organisation, even through a crisis. It provides a conversational interface, answering complex questions with precise authorised guidance, grounded in your company’s verifiable knowledge. Which can be used directly, or referenced by AI Agents to improve customer support.

This stands in stark contrast to the current reality for many organizations.

Now, scale the problem to an industrial level. A company building complex medical machines might depend on a handful of experts. This creates a fragile system: expensive training programs and the constant risk that a single retirement could trigger a crisis.

The traditional solution is to rely on ‘flat’ manuals. These cannot record the complex, branching, decision-making expertise needed, becoming a single point of failure for the entire organization. This is documentation hell - where critical knowledge is scattered, or worse, unrecorded, making support difficult, leaving customers feeling abandoned.

This Website is One Single Guide

This website isn’t just describing Docs Assembler — it is Docs Assembler. Every piece of text has been dynamically assembled on the fly from the DocumentationHell guide. This is how you create and maintain expansive documentation with unparalleled ease and precision.

This challenge manifests everywhere

It’s not just about writing documentation — it’s about maintaining it. The symptoms are universal:

  • Sprawling, duplicated content - that multiplies across guides, manuals, and wikis, making it impossible to know what’s accurate.
  • Bug-prone updates: - you make a critical edit in one place, only to miss that same information duplicated in other files, instantly introducing inconsistencies.
  • Brittle, unmanageable docs - that collapse under their own weight when you try to document complex, branching real-world scenarios.

When the Stakes Are Highest

The true power of this approach is that it scales.

Consider managing emergencies at an oil refinery. The variables are endless: fires, explosions, earthquakes, power loss, IT failures, medical crises. The number of internal teams — incident commanders, operators, maintenance, security, medical, PR, IT, legal, HR — is large, and each needs tailored, timely steps. External stakeholders like emergency services and media introduce more jurisdiction-specific requirements. Add in site variability like equipment locations and local laws, and the complexity is staggering.

Now imagine capturing all of that in a single, maintainable system. Each team builds and maintains their own domain-specific maps. The result is a unified, validated, and always up-to-date source of truth that can guide an entire organisation through a crisis.
